message: Need N-01: SHL returns on tangible capital

need.label: SHL returns on tangible capital
need.question: For each fiscal year from FY2018 to FY2026, what are SHL's NOPAT inputs (EBIT, amortization from IFRS 3 purchase price allocation, income tax and tax rate, income attributable to non-controlling interests) and TICAP inputs (total assets, cash, goodwill, non-interest-bearing current liabilities)?
need.rationale: ROTIC is NOPAT over average TICAP. SHL listed in March 2018, so balance sheets exist from Sep 30, 2018 and at most eight years of average TICAP (FY2019 to FY2026) can be built. That is short of the ten-year window, so the score must carry low confidence. The same SHL figures are the company side of rotic_vs_peers.

message: Need N-02: Peer returns on tangible capital

need.label: Peer returns on tangible capital
need.question: What are NOPAT and TICAP inputs for GE HealthCare and Philips over the same years, taken from their SEC XBRL filings and computed the same way as for SHL?
need.rationale: The framework compares like with like. Both peers file with the SEC, so code reads tagged audited figures with no agent. Their fiscal years end on Dec 31, three months after SHL's, and Philips reports under IFRS in euros while GE HealthCare reports under US GAAP in dollars. ROTIC is a ratio, so the currency does not matter, but the year offset has to be stated.

message: Need N-03: Revenue series by year and segment

need.label: Revenue series by year and segment
need.question: How has SHL's revenue grown each year since FY2018, in total and by segment, on a reported and a comparable basis?
need.rationale: Secular growth starts from the company's own revenue record. The segment series breaks on Oct 1, 2025: Imaging, Diagnostics, Varian and Advanced Therapies ran to the end of FY2025, and FY2026 reports Imaging, Precision Therapy and Diagnostics. Any segment trend has to say so.

message: Need N-04: End-market growth and decline risks

need.label: End-market growth and decline risks
need.question: How fast are SHL's addressable markets growing, what growth does management expect for FY2027, and does anything point to secular decline, such as diagnostics weakness in China or tariffs?
need.rationale: Secular growth scores -1 only on evidence of decline ahead. The annual report sizes the markets and names the long-term trends, the results release gives the FY2027 outlook, and outside coverage checks whether the Diagnostics problems look structural.

message: Need N-05: Debt, leases and pensions against earnings

need.label: Debt, leases and pensions against earnings
need.question: What are SHL's financial debt, lease liabilities, pension provisions, net debt and net debt to EBITDA, how much of the debt is owed to the Siemens Group, and what happens to those loans when Siemens AG deconsolidates SHL?
need.rationale: Leverage weighs debt, leases and pension obligations against earnings power. Most of SHL's debt is loans from the Siemens Group, and the FY2025 report says those loans can be terminated early once Siemens AG holds less than half the votes, so the changed shareholder structure is a leverage question.

message: Need N-06: Free cash flow against what it must fund

need.label: Free cash flow against what it must fund
need.question: What free cash flow does SHL generate, and what must it cover over the next five years: debt maturities, drawn credit facilities and dividends?
need.rationale: Liquidity scores free cash flow coverage of five-year maturities, facilities and dividends (above 2x is +1, below 1x is -1). That needs the cash flow statement, the maturity analysis, the credit facility note and the dividend proposal.

message: Need N-07: R&D spend, pipeline and forecastability

need.label: R&D spend, pipeline and forecastability
need.question: How much does SHL spend on R&D, what is the pipeline focused on, and how predictable is the business going into FY2027?
need.rationale: Research stage is about the analyst's own coverage history, which no public source can answer, so that part stays a declared gap unless the analyst supplies it. This need gives the drafter the R&D and outlook evidence for the other side of the anchor, whether the company is too hard to forecast.

message: Source S-001 (priority, rank 1): Siemens Healthineers Annual Report FY2025

source.title: Siemens Healthineers Annual Report FY2025
source.rationale: The latest audited statements and notes: income statement, balance sheet, cash flows, goodwill, intangibles, financial debt, credit facilities, maturities, segments, dividends, R&D and the subsequent-events note on the Siemens AG deconsolidation. FY2026 statements are not audited yet, so this is the base for everything the release does not cover.

message: Source S-002 (priority, rank 2): Siemens Healthineers Q4 FY2026 earnings release and financial results

source.title: Siemens Healthineers Q4 FY2026 earnings release and financial results
source.rationale: The FY2026 figures, released Nov 5, 2026: full-year income statement, balance sheet at Sep 30, 2026, cash flows, the EBITDA and purchase price allocation reconciliation by the new segments, the FY2027 outlook and the dividend proposal. BOFFIN treats a filing older than the last full fiscal year as stale, so this release is the FY2026 base until the annual report comes out on Nov 26, 2026. It is the full PDF linked from the press release, which also mentions the different shareholder structure and the Diagnostics carve-out.

message: Source S-003 (priority, rank 5): Siemens Healthineers Annual Report FY2023

source.title: Siemens Healthineers Annual Report FY2023
source.rationale: ROTIC history: income statements for FY2023 and FY2022, balance sheets at Sep 30, 2023 and 2022, and the purchase price allocation line from the segment reconciliation. The FY2025 report only goes back to Sep 30, 2024.

message: Source S-004 (priority, rank 6): Siemens Healthineers Annual Report FY2021

source.title: Siemens Healthineers Annual Report FY2021
source.rationale: ROTIC history: FY2021 and FY2020 income statements, balance sheets at Sep 30, 2021 and 2020, and the purchase price allocation line. FY2021 includes the Varian acquisition, which roughly doubled goodwill, so the ROTIC series has a step here.

message: Source S-005 (priority, rank 7): Siemens Healthineers Annual Report FY2019

source.title: Siemens Healthineers Annual Report FY2019
source.rationale: ROTIC history back to listing: FY2019 and FY2018 income statements, balance sheets at Sep 30, 2019 and 2018, and the amortization of intangibles acquired in business combinations. These years predate IFRS 16, so the lease interest add-back cannot be built the same way. Lowest relevance of the priority sources.

message: Source S-006 (tier_2, rank 1): Reuters via Euronext: Siemens Healthineers begins carve-out of diagnostics unit amid China weakness

source.title: Reuters via Euronext: Siemens Healthineers begins carve-out of diagnostics unit amid China weakness
source.rationale: Independent wire coverage of the FY2026 results, published Nov 5, 2026: slower FY2027 growth, China weakness in Diagnostics, the carve-out into Olyrian Diagnostics by mid-2028 and an analyst's view. It cross-checks the release, and any figure it gives must not contradict the tier 1 number. Fetched after every priority source.

message: Source S-007 (priority, rank 3): SEC XBRL company facts: GE HealthCare (peer)

source.title: SEC XBRL company facts: GE HealthCare (peer)
source.rationale: The closest listed peer in imaging. Audited US GAAP figures tagged by filing and period from its 10-Ks (FY2022 to FY2025, Dec year end), read by code with no agent: operating income, intangible amortization, taxes, assets, cash, goodwill, current liabilities.

message: Source S-008 (priority, rank 4): SEC XBRL company facts: Philips (peer)

source.title: SEC XBRL company facts: Philips (peer)
source.rationale: A second European health technology peer that files a 20-F with the SEC. IFRS figures in euros tagged by period (FY2020 to FY2025, Dec year end), read by code with no agent. Philips is more diversified than SHL, so it is the weaker comparison of the two.

source.rationale: An investing blog post from Aug 5, 2026 on the Q3 outlook cut and the Diagnostics weakness. Low trust: automated commentary, never the only support for a number, scanned by Guardrails before any agent reads it.

item.statement: R&D activities focus on artificial intelligence, sensors, and robotics, with innovations in imaging quality optimization, AI-supported image reconstruction, diagnostics, cancer therapy platforms, and endovascular robotics.

citations.quote: Artificial intelligence ("AI"), sensors, and robotics are focal points of our R&D activities. AI has been an integral part of key innovations developed by Siemens Healthineers for several years. In our portfolio of products and solutions, we employ AI successfully for data analysis and interpretation, decision-making, intelligent robot control, and automation. Our innovation activities in the Imaging segment are focused on optimizing image quality while simultaneously shortening scan times, as well as on AI-supported image reconstruction and automated analysis. In the Diagnostics segment we are further focusing on clinical and technical innovations to meet current and future medical needs and harness the latest technology trends. At Varian, we are transforming the fight against cancer and related diseases by integrating imaging and therapy into a single, connected platform that enables more precise, personalized, and effective care. In the Advanced Therapies segment, we are working to develop innovations in clinical processes, imaging and image-guidance based on the smart combination of mechatronics and digitalization. Another focus area is the development of an endovascular robotics platform for neurovascular care.

item.text: For Siemens Healthineers, EBIT, amortization from IFRS 3 purchase price allocation and the effective tax rate are available for fiscal years 2022 to 2026, and total assets, cash, goodwill and current liabilities for computing TICAP are available at fiscal year-ends 2018, 2019, 2022, 2023, 2025 and 2026. NOPAT is computed as EBIT plus the purchase price allocation amortization add-back (reported as a negative figure) less taxes at the year's effective rate less income attributable to non-controlling interests; no equity income or operating-lease interest component is reported, so neither is included. TICAP is computed as total assets less cash less goodwill, leaving non-interest-bearing current liabilities out because they are not separately disclosed; trade payables are not used because they are not reported at every year-end needed, so TICAP is a proxy of total assets less cash less goodwill. For FY2022, NOPAT is EBIT less the amortization add-back, less tax at the year's effective rate, less non-controlling interest income; FY2022 ROTIC uses FY2022 year-end TICAP alone as a proxy for the average, because FY2021 year-end total assets, cash and goodwill are unavailable; FY2022 ROTIC is 9.6%. For FY2023, NOPAT uses EBIT, the amortization add-back and non-controlling interest income, with average TICAP from FY2022 and FY2023 year-end balances; FY2023 ROTIC is 7.4%. For FY2025, amortization add-back and non-controlling interest data exist but FY2024 total assets, cash and goodwill are missing, so FY2025 ROTIC uses FY2025 year-end TICAP alone as a proxy for the average; FY2025 ROTIC is 10.9%. For FY2026, no purchase price allocation amortization figure is reported for the year, so NOPAT is EBIT less tax at the year's effective rate less non-controlling interest income, with average TICAP from FY2025 and FY2026 year-end balances; FY2026 ROTIC is 9.5%. Across the four fiscal years that could be computed (FY2022, FY2023, FY2025, FY2026), the mean ROTIC is 9.4%.

GE HealthCare's NOPAT is computed as operating income plus amortization of intangible assets less taxes at the year's effective rate, since no equity income, operating-lease interest component or non-controlling interest is given in the data. TICAP is computed as total assets less cash less goodwill less current liabilities net of short-term debt, as a proxy for non-interest-bearing current liabilities, leaving out any non-interest-bearing liabilities not separable from short-term debt. For FY2023, NOPAT uses operating income and amortization, with average TICAP from FY2022 and FY2023 year-end balances; FY2023 ROTIC is 26.8%. For FY2024, NOPAT uses operating income and amortization, with average TICAP from FY2023 and FY2024; FY2024 ROTIC is 26.5%. For FY2025, NOPAT uses operating income and amortization, with average TICAP from FY2024 and FY2025; FY2025 ROTIC is 25.2%. Across the three fiscal years computed, the mean ROTIC is 26.2%.

Philips' NOPAT is computed as operating income plus amortization of intangible assets less taxes at the year's effective rate, since no equity income, operating-lease interest component or non-controlling interest is given in the data; in FY2022 and FY2023 both operating income and the pre-tax income used for the tax rate are negative. TICAP is computed as total assets less cash less goodwill less current liabilities net of short-term debt, as a proxy for non-interest-bearing current liabilities. For FY2023, operating income and amortization are used with an effective tax rate derived from a negative pre-tax income and a negative tax expense; average TICAP uses FY2022 and FY2023 year-end balances; FY2023 ROTIC is 3.8%. For FY2024, operating income and amortization are used, with average TICAP from FY2023 and FY2024; FY2024 ROTIC is -33.4%. For FY2025, operating income and amortization are used, with average TICAP from FY2024 and FY2025; FY2025 ROTIC is 18.1%. Across the three fiscal years computed, the mean ROTIC is -3.8%.

Revenue grew from €13,429 million in fiscal year 2018 to €23,630 million in fiscal year 2026, a cumulative increase of 76.0% over the eight-year span. Growth was positive in every year of the series, with fiscal 2026 revenue of €23,630 million up from €23,375 million in fiscal 2025.

Comparable revenue growth was 5.9% in fiscal year 2025 and 4.0% in fiscal year 2026. Management expects comparable revenue growth of between 4.0% and 5.0% for fiscal year 2027 compared with fiscal year 2026, an outlook that assumes the current macroeconomic environment including the interest rate level remains largely unchanged and excludes potential charges from tariff changes and supply chain resilience issues.

By segment, the global addressable market was slightly more than €31 billion for Imaging, approximately €37 billion for Diagnostics, more than €6 billion for Varian and over €7 billion for Advanced Therapies in fiscal year 2025. For fiscal year 2026, moderate growth was assumed in Imaging markets overall, strong growth in the Precision Therapy segment market, and slight growth in the Diagnostics market, with a temporary market downturn in China expected to continue, as centralized volume-based public procurement expansion and government price control measures have an adverse impact on the Diagnostics market. Diagnostics comparable revenue declined 4.2% in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026, and Siemens Healthineers experienced a weaker-than-expected recovery in its Diagnostics division, particularly in China and legacy platforms, in fiscal year 2026, with the biggest risk identified as Diagnostics pressures lingering longer than expected and keeping group growth and margins below shareholder expectations.

Longer-term demand drivers cited include the number of over-60s projected to more than double by 2050, access to medical care remaining insufficient for over half of the world population, and a continued shift toward outpatient care expected in the United States. Trade restrictions could have an adverse impact on the medical technology sector, and China is executing its 14th Five Year Plan with a focus on building a tiered hospital system and driving affordable healthcare via cost control measures including volume-based and centralized public procurement systems, while also focusing on promoting localization and local innovation for government procurement activities.

At September 30, 2025, SHL's reported financial debt (short-term plus long-term) was €755 million, pension provisions were €488 million, and net debt including pensions was €12,472 million, equal to 2.8 times EBITDA. Liabilities to the Siemens Group from financing activities totaled €14,038 million (€3,183 million current and €10,855 million non-current), which made up the large majority of total debt-like obligations of €15,281 million (financial debt plus Siemens Group financing liabilities plus pensions). Interest expenses on the Siemens Group financing arrangements were €335 million in fiscal year 2025.

A year later, at September 30, 2026, SHL's reported financial debt (short-term plus long-term) was €866 million and pension provisions were €333 million. Liabilities to the Siemens Group were €2,932 million current and €10,943 million non-current, totaling €13,875 million, which remained the large majority of total debt-like obligations of €15,074 million (financial debt plus Siemens Group liabilities plus pensions). Cash and cash equivalents were €2,542 million at the same date.

Of the non-current Siemens Group financing liabilities of €10,855 million at September 30, 2025, €10,837 million was loans, including five US dollar-denominated loans with carrying amounts of €1,438 million, €1,059 million, €1,482 million, €1,266 million and €843 million, and a €500 million euro loan maturing in fiscal year 2028; together these six identified loans total €6,588 million. If Siemens AG's shares or voting rights in Siemens Healthineers AG fall below 50% plus one share, financing agreements between Siemens Healthineers AG and the Siemens Group provide for early termination rights for Siemens AG or affiliated companies, with market value compensation for some loans, and loans whose market value at September 30, 2025 was, according to preliminary estimates, significantly below book value carry a compensation clause for early termination whose currently estimated one-off positive effect could be offset by correspondingly higher financing expenses in later periods due to currently higher market interest rates. Siemens AG announced on November 12, 2025 that it intends to deconsolidate Siemens Healthineers and transfer 30% of the Siemens Healthineers shares to Siemens AG shareholders.

Siemens Healthineers generated free cash flow of €2,714 million in fiscal year 2025 and around €2.4 billion (€2,446 million) in fiscal year 2026. Over the two years free cash flow summed to €5,160 million.

Five-year debt maturities due fiscal years 2026 through 2030 (non-derivative financial liabilities of €6,243 million in fiscal year 2026, €2,098 million in fiscal year 2027, and €5,158 million in fiscal years 2028 to 2030) total €13,499 million. Adding the proposed fiscal year 2026 dividend of €1,118 million gives a combined five-year funding requirement of €14,617 million. Fiscal year 2026 free cash flow of €2,446 million (D-343) covers about 16.7% of this amount, and the two-year fiscal 2025-2026 free cash flow sum of €5,160 million (c1) covers about 35.3% of it.

Siemens Healthineers also has liabilities to the Siemens Group of €3,457 million due in fiscal year 2026, €1,932 million due in fiscal year 2027, and €4,918 million due in fiscal years 2028 to 2030, totaling €10,307 million over the period. If Siemens AG's shareholding in Siemens Healthineers AG falls below 50% plus one share, financing agreements with the Siemens Group provide for early termination rights for Siemens AG or affiliated companies, with market value compensation for some loans; loans whose market value as of September 30, 2025 was according to preliminary estimates significantly below book value include a compensation clause for early termination.

Research and development expenses were €1,918 million in fiscal year 2024, €1,958 million in fiscal year 2025 and €1,969 million in fiscal year 2026. R&D expenses equaled 8% of revenue in fiscal year 2025. R&D expenses grew from fiscal year 2024 to fiscal year 2026 by 2.7%. At fiscal year-end 2025, the R&D workforce exceeded 13,000 employees and the company held more than 16,000 granted patents.

Across the four fiscal years that could be computed (FY2022, FY2023, FY2025, FY2026) out of the ten the criterion asks for, SHL's mean ROTIC is 9.4%, close to but just below the 15% threshold for a plus-one score and well above the 10% minus-one bar, so the score is set at the midpoint. Several years (FY2024, and years before FY2022) could not be computed because total assets, cash and goodwill were not all available in the data, and the FY2022 and FY2025 computations use year-end TICAP as a proxy for the average because the prior year-end balance was unavailable, so confidence is low.

On the same proxy method (operating EBIT plus acquired-intangible amortization less tax at the effective rate, over total assets less cash less goodwill and, where available, net of non-interest-bearing current liabilities), SHL's mean ROTIC across FY2022, FY2023, FY2025 and FY2026 is 9.4%, versus GE HealthCare's mean of 26.2% across FY2023-FY2025 and Philips' mean of -3.8% across FY2023-FY2025. SHL's figure is below GE HealthCare's but above Philips', and the three series are not perfectly comparable: GE HealthCare's and Philips' TICAP proxies net current liabilities of short-term debt (not available for SHL), SHL's fiscal year ends three months earlier, and Philips' FY2022-FY2023 figures reflect negative operating income and pre-tax income.

Revenue rose every year from €13,429 million in fiscal year 2018 to €23,630 million in fiscal year 2026, a cumulative increase of 76.0% (c1), comparable growth was 5.9% in fiscal year 2025 and 4.0% in fiscal year 2026, and management guides to between 4.0% and 5.0% comparable growth in fiscal year 2027 (c2). Segment addressable markets are sized at roughly €31 billion (Imaging), €37 billion (Diagnostics), over €6 billion (Varian) and over €7 billion (Advanced Therapies), with moderate-to-strong market growth assumed across most segments for fiscal year 2026, and secular demand drivers such as an aging population and underserved global healthcare access are cited (c3, c4). The one area of weakness is Diagnostics, where a temporary China market downturn and a weaker-than-expected recovery pressured comparable growth, including a 4.2% comparable revenue decline in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026, and this is flagged as the biggest company risk; however, this is described as temporary/China-specific rather than evidence of secular decline across the group, so the evidence does not meet the bar for a -1 score.

Net debt including pensions stood at €12,472 million, 2.8 times EBITDA at September 30, 2025 (c1), and debt-like obligations were €15,074 million at September 30, 2026 against cash of €2,542 million (c2). Liabilities to the Siemens Group made up 91.9% of total debt-like obligations in FY2025 and 92.0% in FY2026 (c1, c2), and most of the identified loans are US dollar-denominated and subject to early-termination and market-value compensation clauses once Siemens AG's stake falls below 50% plus one share, a change already announced for a 30% share transfer (c3). This concentration of leverage in related-party loans with a change-of-control trigger, combined with net debt to EBITDA near 3 times, weighs negatively.

Fiscal year 2026 free cash flow of €2,446 million (c1) covers about 16.7% of the five-year non-derivative financial liability maturities plus the fiscal year 2026 dividend (€14,617 million, c2), far below the 1x threshold for the minus-one anchor. Even combining two years of free cash flow (€5,160 million, c2) covers only about 35.3% of that five-year need (c2). Siemens Healthineers also carries separate liabilities to the Siemens Group of €10,307 million due through fiscal year 2030 (c3), with early termination rights for Siemens AG if its shareholding falls below 50% plus one share, which could accelerate some of this debt. Coverage is well under 1x on these figures.
